protocol: Held-out testable items where the reader recorded no run count. For each item where the released pipeline attaches a count, a second reader with the whole paper decided whether the paper states a count that applies to the boxed table.

adjudicated.evidence: Boxed cell: Table 1 (p.7), D'Kitty / UniSO-T cell 243.428 +- 20.137. The pipeline's '16' comes from Appendix G (p.35), inside a quoted EoH prompt that paraphrases the Design-Bench task description of Ant/D'Kitty: "To evaluate the ground-truth value for a given design, we run robotic simulation in MuJoCo for 100 timesteps, averaging 16 independent trials. These parameters are chosen to reduce stochasticity and allow the simulator to run in a minimal amount of time." The same value recurs only as oracle metadata in the JSON on p.44: "evaluation_trials": 16, "simulation_length": 100. This is the number of MuJoCo rollouts the ORACLE averages to score ONE design in the two robot-morphology tasks; it is not the number of seeds/runs that produced the mean +- std in this table (and it would not apply to Superconductor, TF Bind or GTOPX rows at all). No run/seed count is stated anywhere for the results tables: Sec. 4.1 'Detailed settings' (p.6) gives only epochs (200), batch size (128), BO iterations (200) and 128 final solutions; Appendix B (pp.18-20) gives hyper-parameters only; the only other 'seed' mentions are 'random seed of the data generation procedure as 1' (p.21, dataset generation), 'exact evaluation over multiple seeds' (p.21, reason for excluding NAS), and the real-world task seeds '100 for LunarLander, 100 for RobotPush, and 150 for Rover' (p.22, task-instance seeds, not repetitions). No caption or sentence says 'averaged over N runs/seeds'.

Page 7, Section 6 (comparative experiments): "For each dataset, we repeat the experiments 20 times and compute the average performance. The true number of clustering class is chosen as k for each dataset. Three performance metrics are selected to evaluate the methods: NMI, ARI, and Purity, and larger value indicates better performance. Table 1 reports the comparisons based on the NMI metric, while the results for ARI and Purity are provided in Appendix E.3." Appendix E.3 (page 24) confirms Table 4 is those ARI results: "In the appendix, we continue to demonstrate the performance of the algorithm on ARI and Purity. As can be seen in Table 4 and Table 5, on both ARI and Purity, our method consistently leads against the compared methods across all datasets." No other seed/run/trial count appears anywhere in the paper; the only other numeric settings are ensemble size m (e.g. m=10 base clusterings, E.6), which is not a run count. The mean±std cells in Table 4 (boxed D5 = 67.5±5) are therefore over the same 20 repetitions as Table 1.

Table 8 (Appendix K, p.25; caption p.25, text p.24) has no run statement of its own -- Appendix K only says 'We set the number of ensembles to 1 for all different configurations (light-tailed kernel, heavy-tailed kernel, dual-tailed kernel). Our findings (Table 8) reveal ...' (p.24). It therefore inherits the paper-wide protocol, stated twice: Sec. 8.1, p.9: 'Each experiment is repeated on three splits and averaged, with performance measured by AUC-ROC and AUC-PR ... five seeds ({0,1,2,100,1000}) are used for stochastic methods'; Appendix H 'Experiment Setup', p.19: 'We repeat all experiments on three different splits and report average results. ... For stochastic methods, five random seeds {0,1,2,100,1000} are used'. 'All experiments' covers the Appendix K ablation, so each Table 8 cell is an average over 3 splits -> applicable_n = 3. Caveats: (a) the only '3' among the pipeline's pattern matches is p.23 'Each size is run three times with different random seeds, and we report the average wall-clock time' -- that sentence belongs to the Appendix J scalability/runtime experiment (Figure 2), not Table 8, so the pipeline reached the right number via the wrong sentence (the applicable 'three splits' sentence was not among its matches); (b) WSAD-DT is a stochastic deep method, so the 'five seeds for stochastic methods' clause also applies, and the paper never says whether the reported average additionally spans the 5 seeds (3 splits x 5 seeds = 15 runs per cell) -- the explicitly 'averaged' repetition count is the 3 splits, which is what is reported here.
adjudicated.parenthesised_values_are: ranks (1)/(2)/(3) per row across the three kernel configurations, not error bars; the table reports point averages only (no std/CI), and the bottom rows are 'AVG Rank' and Wilcoxon p-values -- so a variance-based per-cell test is not supportable regardless of n

All the experiments were repeated 10 times to get the mean value." We follow [36] or their configurations to tune the hyperparameters for better performance. We report the mean and standard deviation over five independent runs." This is the paper's only run-count statement and is stated as the protocol for the whole evaluation (17 datasets, all baselines). The boxed cell is the 'Ours' Roman-Empire entry of appendix Table 6 (page 24), 93.03 +/- 0.33; the entire 'Ours' row of Table 6 (45.53+/-1.76, 44.34+/-4.39, 55.86+/-0.13, 93.03+/-0.33, 99.45+/-0.12, 79.55+/-0.31) is numerically identical to the G2Former row of main-text Table 2 (page 7), which is directly governed by the five-run statement.
